title: Smart Dispatch: Dependency-Aware Task Routing
description: Add --sequential execution mode to /dispatch for dependent tasks. Eliminates merge conflicts and ceremony overhead for sequential work. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-22-feat-smart-dispatch-dependency-routing-plan.md

title: Verify Agent tool behavior without isolation param
description:
## Goal
Verify that the Agent tool WITHOUT `isolation: "worktree"` shares the orchestrator's filesystem and working directory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Spawn an Agent without isolation param, have it create a file, verify the file exists in the orchestrator's working directory
- [ ] Verify the agent sees the orchestrator's current branch and recent commits
- [ ] Document behavior: does the agent get its own context window? Can it run skills?
- [ ] If Agent without isolation does NOT share filesystem: document the fallback (orchestrator runs worker inline)

## Target Files
- None (verification task, produces documentation only)

## Notes
This is the one UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION in the plan. Must complete before implementation.

title: Add --sequential flag to /dispatch
description:
## Goal
Add `--sequential` flag to /dispatch that dispatches tasks one at a time without worktree isolation.

## Changes
1. Add `--sequential` to argument parsing section
2. Add Step 2.1: Validate sequential prerequisites (not on main, working branch exists)
3. Support `--sequential --through <id>`: walk deps backward via `bd dep tree <id> --status=open`
4. Step 4: Show [SEQ] or [PAR] per task in confirmation summary
5. Step 5: Two spawn paths:
   - Parallel (default): existing worktree behavior, unchanged
   - Sequential: loop through tasks, Agent(no isolation, run_in_background: false), wait between
6. Sequential worker prompt: include EXECUTION_MODE: sequential, instruct /finish-task --direct
7. Step 6: Reflect execution mode in post-dispatch summary

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `/dispatch --sequential <task-ids>` dispatches tasks one at a time in foreground
- [ ] `/dispatch --sequential --through <id>` resolves dependency chain and dispatches in order
- [ ] Workers spawned without `isolation: "worktree"`
- [ ] Workers spawned with `run_in_background: false`
- [ ] Worker prompt includes EXECUTION_MODE: sequential
- [ ] Default parallel dispatch behavior completely unchanged
- [ ] Dispatch refuses if on main/master branch with --sequential

## Target Files
- skills/dispatch/SKILL.md

title: Add --direct flag to /finish-task + fail-fast merge
description:
## Goal
Add `--direct` flag to /finish-task that skips PR creation, code review, and merge. Also add fail-fast on merge conflicts in worktree mode.

## Changes
1. Parse `--direct` flag from $ARGUMENTS (alongside task ID)
2. Steps 1-10: unchanged in both modes
3. Step 11 (Create PR): wrap in conditional — skip if --direct
4. Step 11a (Code Review): wrap in conditional — skip if --direct
5. Step 12 (Merge PR + Cleanup): two changes:
   - If --direct: skip entirely
   - If worktree mode: add fail-fast on merge conflict. Output: 'MERGE CONFLICT: Do not retry. Report this to the orchestrator.' and STOP.
6. Steps 13-17 (summary, close, notify): unchanged — session summaries MUST still be generated
7. Step 17 (notify): note 'Direct mode, no PR' in the notification

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `/finish-task <id> --direct` skips steps 11, 11a, 12
- [ ] `/finish-task <id> --direct` still generates session summary (steps 14-15)
- [ ] `/finish-task <id> --direct` still closes task in beads (step 9)
- [ ] `/finish-task <id> --direct` still pushes to remote (step 8)
- [ ] Worktree mode: merge conflict triggers immediate stop with clear message
- [ ] Worktree mode: NO retry of merge strategies (no cherry-pick, no rebase attempts)
- [ ] Default (no --direct) behavior completely unchanged

## Target Files
- skills/finish-task/SKILL.md

title: Update /start-task to skip branch creation on working branch
description:
## Goal
When a worker is in direct/sequential mode on a non-main working branch, /start-task should NOT create a new task-specific branch. The worker should commit directly to the orchestrator's working branch.

## Changes
1. Step 7 (Branch Isolation): Add condition — if current branch is not main/master AND the worker was dispatched in sequential mode, skip branch creation
2. The worker prompt from /dispatch --sequential will indicate the branch to use

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Worker on milestone/m4 in sequential mode: stays on milestone/m4, no new branch
- [ ] Worker on main: still creates task branch (existing safety behavior unchanged)
- [ ] Worker in worktree (parallel mode): still creates task branch (unchanged)

## Target Files
- skills/start-task/SKILL.md

title: Add --sequential support to /auto-run
description:
## Goal
Add --sequential flag support to /auto-run so the autonomous loop can dispatch sequential chains.

## Changes
1. Argument parsing: add --sequential flag
2. Section 2 (First Dispatch): pass --sequential to /dispatch when flag is set
3. Step D (Dispatch Next): when --sequential, dispatch one task at a time via /dispatch --sequential
4. Checkpoint: add execution_mode field to config section
5. Note: sequential workers are foreground (run_in_background: false), so orchestrator blocks until each completes. No background notification loop needed for sequential tasks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /auto-run --sequential dispatches tasks sequentially
- [ ] Checkpoint tracks execution_mode
- [ ] --resume restores execution_mode from checkpoint
- [ ] Mid-chain failure: stops chain, reports, moves to next ready batch
- [ ] Can mix with non-sequential: --sequential only affects how dispatch is called

## Target Files
- skills/auto-run/SKILL.md
